# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 75 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 48 | **Source Image:** source-texts/coptic/GTH_075_page_001.jpg

---

## Saying 75

**1** Jesus said: "Many are standing at the door, but it is the solitary ones who will enter the bridal chamber."

---

**Consensus Notes (SOPHIA):**

**"Solitary ones"** — *monachos* is the Thomas keyword for the spiritually unified person — one who has made the two into one (cf. Sayings 4, 16, 22, 49). It is not "monk" (though the Coptic word was later used for monastics) but the undivided, integrated self.

**"Bridal chamber"** — *numphon* preserved: this is a technical term in the Thomas/Valentinian tradition for the highest state of sacred union. PNEUMA's "wedding chamber" is softer but acceptable.

**Theological Note:** The saying is a gatekeeping statement: external proximity (standing at the door) does not equal internal qualification (*monachos*). Only the spiritually unified enter.

**Synoptic Parallels:** Echoes Matthew 25:10-12 (the locked door parable) but without the explicit judgment framing.
